cohort: The study participants were 12,497 singleton pregnant women who delivered at ≥22 weeks of gestation between January 2002 and December 2010.
finding: Pregnancies with macrosomia (birth weight ≥ 4,000 g) were associated with a higher incidence of shoulder dystocia and neonatal asphyxia compared to deliveries with neonatal birth weight of 3,500-3,999 g.
mod_finding: Elective cesarean delivery was more common in the macrosomia group, and the rate of shoulder dystocia was higher in cases of vaginal delivery for macrosomic infants.
